answer: The defense is a slow-drip admission tied to a unique epoch signature: every new key must solve a puzzle seeded by the current round, so a gale of sybils cannot reuse yesterday's work and must burn compute afresh each cycle. To earn, a key must also carry a lantern of verified history—answers graded by peers over many epochs—and a fresh cluster of cedar-stiff identities has none, so it waits at zero weight. Attacker cost scales with both time and compute per identity.
